news.title: The Control Gap: Enterprise AI organizations have an ownership problem, not a technology problem — and most are governing it by hand
news.summary_raw: AI portfolios are expanding far faster than the ability to govern them across enterprises. Most organizations run a contested field of platforms, each claiming to be the “primary” AI layer; few could confidently detect a model drifting or failing in production; and the single most-cited barrier to control is the absence of any one owner accountable for AI across the stack. The result is a widening control gap — ambition and spend racing ahead of visibility, ownership, and cost control — with aut
news.summary: VentureBeat published an article highlighting the 'control gap' in enterprise AI governance, attributing it to ownership issues rather than technological limitations. This means most organizations lack a single accountable owner for AI across their stack.
news.enterprise_use: Review the governance structure of your organization's AI portfolio, assess if a clear owner for AI exists across tools like Google Workspace, JumpCloud, and Freshservice, and consider implementing a unified governance framework to address the widening 'control gap'.

news.title: SkillOpt: Agent skills as trainable parameters
news.summary_raw:
AI agents often fail because their instructions, or skills, are manually modified with no guarantee of improvement. Learn how SkillOpt turns skill editing into a training process, making agent behavior more reliable without changing model weights.
The post SkillOpt: Agent skills as trainable parameters appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has introduced SkillOpt, a technique that turns skill editing into a training process for AI agents, making their behavior more reliable without changing model weights.
news.enterprise_use: While this development doesn't directly apply to IT infrastructure, it's an interesting approach to AI reliability; consider applying similar concepts to improve the robustness of AI-driven automation in your IT workflows.

news.title: Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity
news.summary_raw:
AI agents can't remember past conversations. They must constantly reload or retrieve context, which grows less efficient as tasks get longer and more complex. Memora solves this with a scalable memory system separating what’s stored from how it's retrieved.
The post Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has released Memora, a scalable memory system for AI agents to store and retrieve context from past conversations. Memora solves issues related to loading or retrieving context as tasks get longer and more complex.
news.enterprise_use: While Memora is a research announcement, pay attention to future development and integration of similar memory systems in Microsoft 365, such as improved context switching or recall in chats. Missing an efficient storage solution means slower, more manual workflows, especially in long-term projects with multiple users.
